listenings.text: Eduardo, Nora here. I looked at your two programmes, and here are the numbers. London is older and more famous. Its admission rate is four per cent, the lowest in the country. The classes are bigger: sixty students. Miami is younger and less famous. Its admission rate is eighteen per cent, and the classes are smaller: twelve students. London is more expensive: thirty-one thousand a year, against nineteen. Miami is more convenient for you, because the campus is twenty minutes from your office.

Eduardo, Paulo Rezende. I compared the two ports for the March cargo, and the numbers are clear. Santos is bigger and busier. The freight is cheaper there: nineteen dollars a tonne, against twenty-two. But the queue is longer. The last vessel waited eleven days in Santos and three days in Paranagua. Eleven days cost us more than the freight. Paranagua is smaller, but it is faster, and the road from the farm is better in the rain. My decision is Paranagua.
